newsitem.title: TURKEY: Islamist student attacks Turkish newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Islamist student attacks Turkish newspaper.

text.p: An Islamist student attacked the headquarters of one of the major Turkish newspapers on Monday, injuring two employees, officials at the newspaper said.
Kanal D, the sister television channel of mass circulation Hurriyet daily, showed pictures of the newspaper's glass-fronted entrance pocked with bullet-holes.

The man -- a university student of Islamic studies -- overpowered a guard at the newspaper with a toy gun and a knife, grabbed the guard's gun and went up to the 13th floor of the Hurriyet building, where he shot a cleaner, Kanal D said.
The guard suffered minor injuries in the fray.
State-run Anatolian news agency identified the attacker, who surrendered to police, as 22-year-old Huseyin Vuran.
Hurriyet editor Ertugrul Ozkok said on Kanal D that the gunmen appeared to have been an Islamist opposed to the newspapers' secularist line and that the police were looking into the incident.
He was quick to point a finger at Turkey's ruling politicians, who have been embroiled in a war of words with the media.

"I don't want to blame anyone, and this is the business of the police, but it is a fact that members of the government have increased their statements targeting the Turkish media over the past few days," Ozkok said.
"Such things create an atmosphere in which unpleasant incidents take place," he said.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, has always had an uneasy relationship with the mainstream media and has often blamed the media for its role in a rift between the powerful secularist army and the government.

His conservative coalition partner Tansu Ciller, who has come under attack from the secularist press for forming an alliance with Erbakan's Islamists, has also recently jumped into the ring, accusing the media of turning against her because she cut sizeable incentive loans to media holdings from state banks.
The cleaner shot in the leg by the gunman said the man was looking for Aydin Dogan, the head of Dogan Holding, which owns Hurriyet and Kanal D.
"I told him Dogan was away, and that he had made a wasted trip here. He shot me in the leg," said the cleaner, Huseyin Alkir, in an interview on Kanal D.
Alkir said the gunman said Dogan had "dealt a blow" to Islam. The media has been increasingly aggressive in its criticism of the Islamists and their policies.
The assailant later gave himself up to the police, saying that he achieved his aim, Hurriyet officials said.
